LESSON: WRITING 3.3.1 EYE-HAND CO-ORDINATION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Writing 3.3.1 Eye-hand co-ordination
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.3.1 Eye-hand co-ordination, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why should we look at our books when writing? 2. How do we hold our books and pencils/pens when writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.3.1 Eye-hand co-ordination together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Unity: Fairness as learner shares coloring pencils and crayons with others while coloring.

• Responsibility: Self -drive as learner holds the crayons or coloreds pencils and colors letter sounds without assistance.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social cohesion as learner works with others in harmony, sharing resources and even

assisting one another to color within borders.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Eye hand co-ordination cuts across all learning area as it’s a skill in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive devices fitted with appropriate technology such as hearing aids and amplifiers, Coloring pencils, crayons, board, book or

chart.
